top10.introHtml: Top 10 picks from 55 filtered listings across Cars.com (9), CarGurus (25), and AutoTrader (23). Ranked by reliability, mileage quality, and convertible-specific condition factors. Roadsters and excluded models removed. All prices $7k–$15k within 35 mi of Media, PA (19063). Refresh: 2026-09-12T13:19:54Z

picks.whyGood: The E88 135i houses a twin-turbo 3.0L inline-six (300 hp) in a compact, sharp-handling package. At 48k miles this is a low-mileage example for a 2008. Good Deal badge confirms market value. The 1-series convertible seats four and drops the top on a budget.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle (soft-top motor can stick on E88s). Check for oil leaks at the valve cover and rear main seal — common on N54. Inspect soft-top hydraulic rams for weeping. Rear window seam and headliner for water staining. Turbo boost tubes for cracking.
picks.bottomLine: Best engine in the budget at less than 50k miles — the twin-turbo E88 135i is a driver's car that punches above its price.

picks.whyGood: 34k miles on a 24-year-old V8 W208 CLK suggests a garage queen — that mileage is extraordinary. The 4.3L V8 is smooth, well-proven, and parts are plentiful. No-accidents history confirmed.
picks.whatToVerify: Top operation: W208 soft-tops can develop issues with the top latch and rear window seal at this age regardless of mileage. Check for rubber seal brittleness. Inspect cooling system (W208 coolant hose failures are age-related). Verify A/C function.
picks.bottomLine: 34k miles on a V8 CLK is a unicorn find — inspect the top carefully and you may have a weekend classic that actually runs.

picks.whyGood: 39k miles on a 2012 E88 128i is exceptional — the N52 inline-six is one of BMW's most reliable naturally-aspirated engines. Four proper seats, sharp steering, and this one has never had an accident.
picks.whatToVerify: Top cycle and hydraulic rams (E88 soft-top motors can stick). Oil leaks from valve cover gasket (common on N52). Check cooling system — DISA valve. Inspect rear seat belt mechanism.
picks.bottomLine: Lowest-mileage modern BMW on the list with a bulletproof N52 engine — hard to beat for long-term reliability.

picks.whyGood: The final-year W209 CLK 350 with under 50k miles is a standout. The 3.5L V6 is smooth and reliable, and the W209 soft-top mechanism is one of Mercedes' best. Same mileage also listed on AT confirming availability.
picks.whatToVerify: Top cycle and rear window seam — W209 rear window seals can shrink. Look for rocker panel rust. Verify A/C cold. Check for transmission service history (722.9 5-speed auto benefits from fresh fluid).
picks.bottomLine: Under 50k miles on the last CLK ever built — a refined open-air cruiser at a fair price.

picks.whyGood: Most modern car in the top 10 — the W205 C300 Cabriolet has turbocharged 2.0L, 7-speed auto, and a beautiful retractable soft-top. Great Deal badge at 104k miles. Apple CarPlay, driver assists, and contemporary safety tech.
picks.whatToVerify: Top operation (electric motor + pump — expensive to repair). Check rear quarter window seals. Verify turbo boost at highway speeds. Inspect for oil consumption on M274 engine. CarFax for any frame claims.
picks.bottomLine: A modern C300 Cabriolet with a Great Deal badge is the daily-drivable luxury pick — newer tech than anything else at this price.

picks.whyGood: 2020 S550 Mustang EcoBoost Premium with no-accident history at $12k is tremendous value. The 2.3L EcoBoost makes 310hp, the S550 chassis is excellent, and the soft-top is far better than S197 era. Fred Beans is a reputable dealer.
picks.whatToVerify: Rear convertible top latch wear (common on high-mile S550). Water staining on rear seats from top seal failure. Check 8F35 transmission for smoothness. Rear seat carpet for moisture. Ford recall status.
picks.bottomLine: Most car per dollar on the list — a 2020 no-accident Mustang convertible at $12k from a reputable dealer is hard to argue with.

picks.whyGood: quattro AWD in a convertible is a rarity at this price — you get usable all-weather capability. The B8.5 A5 Cabriolet has a well-sorted soft-top and 220hp 2.0T. Good Deal badge at 111k.
picks.whatToVerify: Top operation (Audi fabric tops can develop leaks at the front header seal). Check for DSG/S-tronic service. Inspect for oil consumption on 2.0T TFSI. Roof drain tubes — must be clear to prevent water intrusion. Timing chain tensioner (known A4/A5 issue).
picks.bottomLine: AWD convertible under $12k with a Good Deal badge — a practical open-air car for the full Pennsylvania driving season.

picks.whyGood: 46k miles on a 1995 XJS 2+2 is genuinely rare — this is a proper British GT with 4 seats and one of the most beautiful cabriolet silhouettes ever made. The 4.0L inline-six is the more reliable choice over the V12. No accidents.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle — XJS fabric tops at this age need careful inspection of the header seals and frame channels. Cooling system (AJ6 overheating can be expensive). Check for Jaguar electrical gremlins. Find a Jaguar specialist for pre-purchase inspection.
picks.bottomLine: The most distinctive car on the list at under $10k — 46k miles makes it a weekend driver worth a specialist PPI.

picks.whyGood: The E46 330Ci is one of the most celebrated driver's cars BMW ever made — 225hp N52 inline-six, nearly perfect 50/50 weight distribution, and handling that's still a benchmark. 84k miles and a Good Deal badge under $8.5k is excellent value.
picks.whatToVerify: Soft-top hydraulic pump and ram cylinders (E46 tops are age-sensitive). Subframe mounting point rust — critical pre-purchase check on E46 convertibles. VANOS unit function. Oil leaks from valve cover and rear main. Cooling system condition.
picks.bottomLine: The E46 330Ci is a future classic already — buy one in good condition now before prices rise further.

picks.whyGood: The IS 250C's retractable hardtop means no soft-top worries — it's weatherproof as a coupe, convertible in 20 seconds. Lexus reliability is legendary and the 2.5L V6 is virtually indestructible. Good Deal badge, clean title, no accidents.
picks.whatToVerify: Hardtop mechanism — check full open/close cycle for smooth operation and no error codes. Hydraulic actuators can be costly. Inspect trunk for water intrusion when closed. Check rear window mechanism seals. IS 250C rear seats are tight but functional.
picks.bottomLine: The only retractable hardtop convertible on the list and the most reliable top mechanism — a worry-free daily driver.

manual10.introHtml: No manual-transmission convertibles could be confirmed from this refresh. Transmission data was unavailable in the structured data returned by Cars.com, CarGurus, and AutoTrader. Several promising candidates (BMW 330Ci, 335i, 135i) are commonly available with manual boxes — if a manual is a priority, filter by transmission on the source site before visiting.

mustangs.introHtml: 5 Ford Mustang convertibles found (2005+ S197/S550 only). All are EcoBoost or V8 variants. The 2010 GT is the only V8 this refresh. No Fox-body or SN95 cars qualified under the 2005+ rule.

picks.whyGood: The only V8 GT on the list — the 4.6L 3-valve makes 315hp and has the genuine Mustang soundtrack. S197 GTs are the benchmark S197 variant. High Priced badge suggests room to negotiate.
picks.whatToVerify: S197 3-valve 4.6: cam-phaser rattle on cold start (2005-2010 known issue — check for rattle at startup). Spring perch rust on rear suspension. Top latch wear at 132k. 8.8 rear axle for clunk on takeoff. Water staining on rear seats.
picks.bottomLine: The V8 GT is the right Mustang to buy — verify the cam phasers and negotiate on the High Priced rating.

picks.whyGood: Final-year S197 at $10,390 with no accidents — the 2014 has the refreshed interior and styling. Good value for a clean no-accident S197 convertible.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch wear. Rear window seam for water intrusion. 8.8 axle clunk. If V6: smooth power delivery check. If V8: cam-phaser rattle on startup. Check airbag recall status.
picks.bottomLine: Best-value Mustang on the list — no-accident S197 under $11k with room to grow as these appreciate.

picks.whyGood: 2020 S550 EcoBoost Premium from Fred Beans (reputable Ford dealer) with no-accident history. S550 is dramatically better than S197 in NVH, chassis stiffness, and top quality. The 2.3T makes 310hp.
picks.whatToVerify: Rear top latch wear at 132k (most common S550 top issue). Rear seat water staining. MT-82 if manual — check shift quality. 8F35 auto smoothness. Check for Takata recall completion.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern Mustang at the most accessible price — the S550 EcoBoost is a legitimate sports car.

picks.whyGood: Great Deal badge confirms price is below market. Nearly identical to rank 3 but listed on CG at slightly higher price — may be same or different car. Great Deal certification adds confidence.
picks.whatToVerify: Same checks as rank 3 above. Compare VIN to rank 3 to verify if same car — if different, both are valid options.
picks.bottomLine: Great Deal badge on a 2020 S550 — solid bang for buck if it's a different VIN from the AT listing above.

picks.whyGood: 2018 S550 EcoBoost Premium — mid-cycle refresh with improved interior and active exhaust option. High Priced badge suggests negotiation room; comparable S550s at less mileage cost the same.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch and rear window seam. Check for active exhaust option (pop/gurgle mode). Same S550 PPI checklist as ranks 3-4. Negotiate given High Priced rating.
picks.bottomLine: Negotiate hard on the High Priced badge and this becomes a reasonable S550 — otherwise rank 3 or 4 are better value.
